name: Spring onion
grown_as: Spring onions (salad onions), sown thickly and pulled young. Most sold in the UK, such as 'White Lisbon', are Allium cepa, a bulb onion pulled early; Japanese bunching types such as 'Ishikura' are Welsh onion, Allium fistulosum, with no bulb at all. They look much the same when pulled. ⚠️ CHECK: William's variety, which decides the Latin name.
habit: Slim plants 20 to 40 cm high, each a straight white shank about 1 cm thick, slightly swollen at the base, with 3 to 6 upright hollow leaves. Year 2: a hollow flower stem 50 to 100 cm, swollen below the middle, with a round head.

leaf.arrangement: In two ranks from the top of the shank
leaf.outline: Long, narrow, hollow round tube, 15 to 35 cm by 0.5 to 1 cm
leaf.base: A sheath wrapping the white shank

flower.form: A round ball of many small star-shaped flowers
flower.colour: Greenish-white to white (yellowish-white in Welsh onion)
flower.centre: Six stamens sticking out beyond the tepals
flower.behind: A short papery spathe folded back under the head
flower.carried: In a dense round umbel at the top of a hollow stem swollen below the middle
flower.season: June to July of the second year

fruit: A dry round head of papery three-lobed capsules with black angular seeds.
seedling: A single thin grass-like seed leaf bent like a hairpin, with the black seed case on its tip, then thin hollow leaves.
winter: Winter-hardy types such as 'White Lisbon Winter Hardy' stand through winter as small upright tufts.

leaf: a long thin hollow round tube
bloom: a round ball of small white star-shaped flowers with stamens sticking out
seed: a small black angular wrinkled seed
seedling: one thin grass-like seed leaf bent like a hairpin, seed case on its tip
young: a row of thin upright plants, each a few hollow leaves
crop: a straight white shank, only slightly swollen at the base, with a tuft of white roots
hollow green leaves from its top
a bunch of several pulled together
flower: a hollow flower stem swollen below the middle
seedhead: a dry round head of papery capsules with black seeds

look_alikes: Leek seedlings have flat, folded leaves fanned in one plane. Chives are much thinner with pink-purple heads. Bulb onions are the same plant left to swell.
